Palette strictly near-black night, warm gold, emerald green and signal red; nothing beige, nothing cream, nothing pastel. Absolutely no people: no characters, no figures, no faces, no hands, no silhouettes, no mannequins. An open comic book lying flat, straight on from above, two pages: the left page is one big panel of a dark theatre with a large blank dark cinema screen facing the viewer; the right page is four stacked wide panels with ink borders: panel one a sealed envelope with a red wax seal on a desk at night, panel two a brass closing bell ringing, panel three a golden ticket on a black velvet podium under a spotlight, panel four a heavy round vault door ajar with gold light inside; each right-hand panel has a wide blank caption plate across its top edge, about a quarter of the panel height and two thirds of its width, black lacquer with a thin gold rim; the left page has one wide blank black caption plate with a gold rim under the cinema screen. Every sign, plate, board, panel, screen, tape, ticket, ribbon and box is completely blank and empty: no text, no letters, no numbers, no digits, no logos, no symbols anywhere in the image.
